summary: Sync has no heal: members move claims and never compare, replay or repair projections from a peer

replay.detail: Heals no longer replay the graph from nothing, and the replay reservation and cooldowns are gone. A full replay still runs for a stale or unhealthy projection, an operation conflict, the first start of a build with a new rule, and a restore.

schema.detail: The unused index claims_batch_claim_id, which only heals read, is dropped with DROP INDEX IF EXISTS on open. No table, column or schema version changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, admission, retention or drop-rule changes.

compatibility.detail: The peer route /v1/peer/heal and the daemon-internal routes /v1/internal/replication/heal/answer and /heal/next are removed. An older member that starts a heal against this build gets an unsigned 404, which it already reports as a peer without the heal route, and backs off. GET /v1/replication/status no longer carries peers[].sync.heal or first_sync.healed; ReplicationReceipt no longer carries heal (it was skipped when false). The metrics st.replication.heals and st.replication.heal.duration and the round attribute st.replication.heal_due are removed. ST3_REPLICATION_HEAL_AFTER_MS has no effect.

manual.detail: No data repair or configuration change.

recovery.detail: A first sync now ends verified at the first exchange where the new member holds and has admitted the same envelopes as a peer; it settles on claims alone and no longer compares graphs. A first sync an earlier build recorded as failed is verified at the next such exchange. A first sync verified across mixed builds stays verified once the builds match, and no longer says a projection comparison is waiting. st fleet wait still refuses a member that admitted envelopes the fleet fenced (admitted beyond a writer's high water), now from those admissions rather than a graph comparison; a projection difference alone no longer fails it and is reported by replication status, replication diff and doctor. Divergence is still reported in replication status, doctor and client pages, but nothing repairs it: it is a projection defect to fix in the build. Rolling back to a build that still has heal is a normal binary rollback, but that build recreates claims_batch_claim_id over the whole claims table when it opens, holding the writer while it does: minutes on an 11.8 GB store.
